findings.problem: The six orange question marks / green ticks in the top-right strip are not tied to the six labels (INPUT, STEPS, COMPARE, STOP, OUTPUT, EDGE CASES). The strip is unlabelled and sits 200 px away from the tags, so the viewer has to count ticks and infer which question each answers; the tick that lands when a part appears is not visibly 'that part's tick'.
findings.fix: Put the question mark and its tick inside each label pill (pill starts as a dashed orange '?', fills with its colour and a drawn tick when answered) and drop the separate strip, or draw a short flash from the strip tick to the pill that was just answered.
findings.evidence: s2@3 (strip: 1 tick, 5 '?', only INPUT on stage), s2@5 (4 ticks vs STOP/STEPS/COMPARE tags in three unrelated places), s2@8.5.

findings.problem: STEPS (above the machine) and COMPARE (below it) both point at the same single purple box, whose only text is 'scan once / x > best?'. A first-time learner cannot tell which line answers STEPS and which answers COMPARE, and the machine looks like one idea with two names. STOP is the only grey tag and its flag pole sits at the end of the list, far from the loop it ends.
findings.fix: Split the machine into two stacked slots, 'scan once' under a STEPS tag and 'x > best?' under a COMPARE tag (both tags on the same side), or place both tags above the box. Tint STOP purple/orange like the other answers so the pole reads as part of the answer.

findings.problem: The invariant's three properties (starts true, stays true, ends useful) are never named on screen. The only hints are a 'first item' tag and a 'holds' pill; the headline says 'stays true' but nothing says it started true or that the last step makes it the answer. The first-time learner sees a tick routine, not the three-part promise that makes a loop trustworthy.
findings.fix: Re-label the first compare tag 'starts true' (with its tick), keep 'holds' but rename it 'stays true' for steps 2 to 7, and label the final 'answer' box 'ends useful' (or add three tiny chips that light in turn). Update caption 3 to 'It starts true, stays true and ends as the answer.'
findings.evidence: s3@3 ('first item'), s3@5 and s3@7 ('holds'), s3@12.5 ('answer', 'return 9').

findings.problem: The tie '9 > 9?' (the second 9 does not beat the first) is the key edge of the compare rule but is shown exactly like any other fail: a grey cross, no emphasis, caption unchanged.
findings.fix: On that step show a small purple '=' or 'tie: keep first' tag beside the cross for about a second.

findings.problem: The grids are (i, j) pairs but no axis, loop code or pseudo-code is shown, and 'work()' is never defined. A first-time learner sees blue squares fill a column, a staircase and a square without knowing which loop is which, why one loop lights only the left column, or what a 'call' is. Scene 3 left the code behind and nothing here replaces it.
findings.fix: Under each panel tag add a one-line code caption at 28 px or more ('for i: work()', 'for i, for j < i: work()', 'for i, for j: work()') or small axis tags 'i' (down) and 'j' (across); say once 'each square = one work() call' alongside the legend (the legend exists but is tiny and at the bottom).
findings.evidence: s4@1.5, s4@4.5, s4@7.5 (no mention of i or j anywhere); caption 1 'Count how many times work() runs' with no work() on screen.

findings.problem: The purple tag '28 is about half of 64' repeats the caption word for word two inches away, so the final second says the same thing twice and wastes the caption slot.
findings.fix: Make the caption carry the next idea ('Both are quadratic: keep the biggest term.') or drop the tag text and keep only the dashed half-square.

findings.problem: The halving loop appears here for the first time (scene 4 never showed it) with its chain 8, 4, 2, 1 already built and a bare counter '3'. Four boxes but a count of three, and the counter pills ('8', '64', '3') have lost the 'work() calls' label scene 4 gave them. The learner cannot see why halving costs 3 calls or what the number counts.
findings.fix: Either add the halving loop as a fourth beat of scene 4, or in scene 5 animate the chain being built with a counter ticking 1, 2, 3 on each arrow and put the unit in the pill ('3 calls'). Prefix the first counters with 'calls:' or reuse the stat card.
findings.evidence: s5@2 (chain of four boxes, counter 3, no label), compare s4@10.5.

findings.problem: Big-O, the scene's headline idea, only arrives at 10.2 s as three pale grey tags (O(n), O(n²), O(log n)) with a 1.5 s hold. The viewer sees x2, x4, +1 land one by one but the names come all at once at the end in the least prominent style.
findings.fix: Reveal each Big-O tag as its signature lands (x2 at 5.2 with O(n), x4 at 7.4 with O(n²), +1 at 10.0 with O(log n)), in the same colour as its signature tag, and keep the caption about the name.
findings.evidence: s5@6, s5@8 (no Big-O), s5@10 (tags appear), s5@11.5.

findings.problem: The 'n = 8 / n = 16' tag floats off-centre (centre x about 432 against column centres 216, 540, 864) and is jammed between the headline and the column tags; 'double n' sits beside it. It reads as stray rather than as the control that drives all three columns.
findings.fix: Centre the n tag at x 540 (over the nested-loops column) with the 'double n' arrow to its right, or place it in the headline row.

findings.problem: Columns change meaning between the two counting scenes. Scene 4 is one loop / inner loop grows / nested loops; scene 5 is one loop / nested loops / halving loop, so 'nested loops' jumps from column 3 to column 2 and the growing inner loop (28 to 120) silently disappears.
findings.fix: Keep the inner-loop panel in scene 5 (28 to 120, about x4.3) or add a quick caption in scene 4 saying why it is dropped; keep nested loops in the same column in both scenes.

findings.problem: No bridge from Big-O to the web: at 50 s the video jumps to four lettered circles and arrows with the caption 'Give every page 25 tokens.' Nothing says the circles are web pages, the arrows are links, or that tokens stand for rank (importance). The title card promised 'How Google ranked the web' but the first PageRank frame never shows the web.
findings.fix: Open with one line and a tiny cue: caption 'Pages link to pages. Rank = importance.' with a small page icon on each node and a link label on one arrow; then 'Give every page 25 tokens of rank.'
findings.evidence: s6@2 (first populated frame), s5@11.5 to s6@0.3 transition.

findings.problem: D's 25 tokens float away at 2.0 to 2.9 s as a faint pink pill while the five link packets are in flight, but the caption that explains it ('D has no links, so its 25 tokens vanish') only shows 4.8 to 6.6 s, two seconds later. The vanishing is the point of the scene and is the least visible thing on screen when it happens.
findings.fix: Hold D's pill until the pour is done, then lift and fade it in a larger red pill at about 4.8 s, in time with the caption and the '-25 lost' tag.
findings.evidence: s6@2.5 (tiny faint '25' near D), s6@5 (caption on screen, nothing moving).

findings.problem: The repair pour is crowded: five grey-link packets and four purple 6.25 packets are in flight at once, 12.5 pills stack on C's ring, and a 6.25 pill collides with the 'pours to all' tag. The idea (D pours to everybody, itself included) is lost in the swarm.
findings.fix: Stagger it: first replay the normal pour dimmed (or skip it and start from 25s), then send D's four purple packets alone, one second later.

findings.problem: The 'total tokens' box resets to 0 and counts up (18.75, 37.5, 81.25, 100) while the caption says 'the total is 100 again', so for a moment it reads 0 next to four full pills. The first tally does the same (62.5 on the way to 75). The running-sum animation is unlabelled and reads as tokens lost.
findings.fix: Keep the label honest: show '+18.75' chips flying into the box, or relabel it 'adding up' while counting and switch to 'total tokens' on the final value; or skip the count and just flip 75 to 100.
findings.evidence: s6@5 (62.5), s6@9.5 and s6@10 (0 then 81.25 with all four pills showing), s6@10.5.

findings.problem: The value pill on A sits on the arrowhead of the C to A link, hiding the head so the link looks undirected (and at 18.75 it covers the whole head). D's starting '25' pill is already red before anything is lost, which breaks the colour role and gives away the ending.
findings.fix: Move A's pill to the left of the node; make D's starting pill blue and turn it red only at the leak.
findings.evidence: s6@4, s6@10.5 (A's pill over the arrowhead); s6@2 (red 25 at D).

findings.problem: After the trap outline lands at about 6.2 s nothing moves for 3.8 s. The held frame is calm but long, and the bars have no numbers, so a viewer has no extra thing to read.
findings.fix: Use the hold for the teaser: a purple dice icon with 'a random jump escapes' fading in, or give the bars the same value pills so A 50, B 25 can be compared.

findings.problem: The scene is the densest in the video: a small graph, three bars, a hops stat, a probability dial with roll dots, a dice and three tags. The surfer itself is a 30 px dot and the nodes are about 70 px, so the thing the viewer should follow is the smallest object on stage; the roll dots pile into an unreadable clump at the 85 per cent edge.
findings.fix: Enlarge the graph and the surfer (roughly 1.4x), drop the roll dots and keep only the dice face and the dial split, or fade the dial out once teleports have been shown (after about 6 s).
findings.evidence: s8@4 (surfer on X barely visible), s8@6 and s8@8 (stacked dots on the dial at x 640-720).

findings.problem: Only one teleport target is ever drawn (a dashed A to X arrow), while the caption says 'a random page'. A first-timer can read teleport as 'go to X'.
findings.fix: Flash a purple halo on all three nodes before the jump lands, or draw faint dashed lines to B and X as well.

findings.problem: The payoff is not said. The last caption ('The shares settle: that is PageRank.') never tells the viewer that X, starved at 0 in scene 7, now has 5 per cent, or that A and B are no longer a trap. The 'via teleport' pill carries it, but it appears over the X bar track in the last second and the caption does not mention it.
findings.fix: Caption: 'X is no longer starved: 5% of visits, all by teleporting.' and bring the 'via teleport' tag in earlier (at 10.0), placed to the right of the bar so it does not cover the track.
findings.evidence: s8@10, s8@11.7 (pill sits on the bar track).

findings.problem: '+ 0.03' is unexplained. '× 0.85' links back to the 85 per cent in scene 8, but nothing ties 0.03 to the 15 per cent teleport share split across five pages. The caption words 'damping' and 'floor' are new jargon. A first-time learner copies the number without knowing where it came from.
findings.fix: Show the sum in the chips ('0.15 ÷ 5 = 0.03') or animate 0.15 splitting into five 0.03 pieces that drop into the cells; caption 'Teleport adds 0.15 ÷ 5 = 0.03 to every cell.'

findings.problem: The row of pills under the matrix ('1 ✓', '1 ✓', ..., '0 ✗') has no label and the captions never mention sums. Viewers will not know they are column sums, or that a 0 under T is the leak the repair fixes.
findings.fix: Add a 28 px 'sum' label at the left end of the row (x 440-500 is free), and make caption 2 'T's column sums to 0, so it pours 0.2 into every page.'

findings.problem: Step 1 fills one column every 0.7 s (P 1.4, Q 2.2, R 2.9, S 3.6), faster than the one-second rule, and the 'to' and 'from' words are small grey labels floating above the headers with no arrows.
findings.fix: Give each column about 1.0 s (shorten step 3 or the final hold) and replace 'to' / 'from' with arrows beside the row and column headers.

findings.problem: The matrix from scene 9 is never used on screen. The loop is shown with 'pour' and 'floor' chips and no matrix, so the viewer cannot tell why scene 9 existed or that each round is one multiplication by that matrix (the storyboard's 'repeated multiplication').
findings.fix: Rename the two chips 'multiply by the matrix' with a small three-band matrix icon (blue links, purple repair/teleport), or show the matrix thumbnail beside the bars with an arrow 'p becomes G p'; caption: 'Each round: multiply by the matrix.'

findings.problem: The caption at 2.2 to 5.4 s wraps to two lines with an orphan word ('floor.') and the final caption ('R ranks first. The same loop ranks billions of pages.') runs edge to edge (x 73 to 1007), so it touches both margins; scene 9's caption is 5 px from the edge.
findings.fix: Shorten both to one comfortable line: 'Each round: pour down the links, add the floor.' and 'R ranks first. The same loop ranks billions.'

findings.problem: The small line chart (260 x 180) has only a 'change' tab: it does not say what changes or that falling is the goal. Its 20 dots overlap into a bead string. The green 'settled' stat shows the number 20, which reads as 20 what? (rounds).
findings.fix: Retitle the tab 'change per round'; shrink the dots to 8 px or draw a line only; label the stat 'settled in' with '20 rounds', or keep 'round' and add a green 'settled' pill.

findings.problem: The three recap mini-animations loop, so the last second is mid-loop and not a resolved state: at 8.8 s card 1 is back at 'best 8', card 2's grid is half full with no x4/+1 tags, and only card 3 is still. The calm complete state (x2, x4, +1 tags and all ticks) is visible only around 4 to 5 s.
findings.fix: Play each mini-animation once, then hold its completed state (all tiles ticked with 9 as the answer, grid full with x2/x4/+1 tags, web settled with R orange) from about 7.8 s to the end of the scene.

findings.problem: Card 1 shows only five of the seven list tiles (3, 8, 1, 9, 4) and never reaches the answer 9, so the invariant card ends on a step that is not the lesson's result. Card 3's web arrows are pale grey (#ddd) and small, hard to read at phone size. The recap leaves out the wish-to-algorithm idea (scene 2) and the matrix (scene 9) without comment.
findings.fix: Show the full seven tiles (or fewer tiles but end on the answer), draw card 3's arrows in the normal grey, and consider a fourth micro-card or a changed headline ('Remember three things').

findings.problem: Figures sit high in several scenes and the lower 120 to 190 px of the stage is empty: scene 2 (content ends y 780), scene 7 (ends y 750), scene 5 until the Big-O tags arrive at 10 s, scene 10 (ends y 815). The captions then float far below the figure.
findings.fix: Shift those figures down 30 to 50 px (scene 3 already does this with DY) so the figure is centred in the 640 px stage.
